title: Transient tiered KV reclaimer and predictable prefetch policy for GPU memory
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a transient tiered reclamation strategy for the paged KV cache and a deterministic prefetch policy that reduces tail latency spikes during oversubscription. Goal: improve 95th/99th percentile latency under mixed-sequence workloads while limiting extra GPU memory churn and avoiding excessive background IO.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile generation latency reduced by >=10% on mixed short/long-sequence benchmark compared to current paged baseline
Spike rate (requests with >2x token-latency) reduced by >=30% under 2.5x oversubscription load
Background GPU-to-host swap IO does not increase median latency by more than 3% in steady-state
New reclaim path has unit and integration tests covering: transient tier allocation, soft-eviction, prefetch hint ingestion, and graceful fallback to full eviction
No regressions on existing functional e2e tests for KV consistency and generation correctness
design_notes: Add an ephemeral 'transient' residency tier inside GPU memory: short-lived KV segments are placed here to avoid immediate eviction churn for hotspots
Prefetch policy driven by a compact heatmap: heatmap buckets derived from recent prefix hit counts and sequence-length-weighted access frequency
Soft-eviction marks segments as candidate for async reclaim but keeps a tiny pinned suffix in GPU to prioritize quick rehydration for imminent reuse
Use a bounded async prefetcher that issues batched host->GPU transfers with coalesced pages to reduce PCIe overhead; backpressure via a token bucket tied to current latency SLO headroom
Integrate with existing slab allocator but add a transient slab class with shorter residency TTL and cheaper metadata operations to minimize lock contention
Fallback: under extreme memory pressure revert prefetch to conservative mode (no prefetch) and enable aggressive compressed-page migration to host-resident compressed slab
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype transient slab class and heatmap counters (unit tests + microbenchmarks)
Phase 2: Implement prefetcher with batched transfer path and token-bucket backpressure; integrate with scheduler hooks
Phase 3: Add soft-eviction marker and small pinned suffix mechanism; exercise in integration harness
Phase 4: Run perf experiments on representative workloads (chatty short-seq, long-context, mixed) and tune thresholds
Phase 5: Rollout canary on dedicated pool with 5% traffic, monitor latency/IO/cost; expand if stable

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Prefetch aggressiveness could increase PCIe traffic and harm other tenants. Mitigation: token-bucket bounded by measured SLO headroom and conservative initial rates in canary
Risk: Soft-eviction may leave too many pinned suffixes, reducing effective capacity. Mitigation: enforce global pinned byte cap and LRU promotion to full-evict when cap exceeded

Risk: Complexity increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep transient tier implementation self-contained and well-instrumented; add metrics for transient residency, reclaim rate, and prefetch throughput
Risk: Possible regressions under very long-context workloads. Mitigation: explicit long-session detection disables transient tier and switches to full-page compaction
